intro: This unit has stories of people who needed help. Hagar was alone in the desert. Moses was far from home. Mary heard surprising news. In each story, the Bible says a messenger from God came close and spoke kindly.

Then come stories about Jesus. He fed hungry people and welcomed children. He sent his friends to all nations. At Pentecost, people heard good news in their own languages. Michael Heiser, a teacher who read the Bible's old languages, saw an invitation for every nation.

In this unit you will retell these stories in order. You will learn words like messenger, holy and nation. You will say what Heiser thought and what other readers think. And you will find ways to help others feel welcome.
bigQuestion: In the Bible stories, how does God come close and invite everyone home?

timeline.t: Hagar is sad and runs into the desert (Genesis 16)
The Angel of the LORD finds Hagar by a spring
Moses watches sheep and sees a burning bush (Exodus 3)
God tells Moses he will help his people
Jesus feeds hungry people and welcomes children (Mark 6 and 10)
Jesus calms the wind and the waves (Mark 4)
Jesus sends his friends to all nations (Matthew 28:19)
At Pentecost, people hear in their own languages (Acts 2)
A crowd from every nation stands together (Revelation 7:9)

words.d: someone who brings words or news from someone else
a special messenger in the Bible stories who speaks for God
special and set apart for God
God's helpers in heaven in the Bible stories; many bring messages
a big group of people with their own land, leaders and often their own language
a Jewish harvest holiday; in Acts 2, the day Jesus' friends spoke in many languages
the different sets of words people use to talk, like English and Spanish
to greet someone gladly and help them feel they belong

test.q: Who met the Angel of the LORD by a spring in the desert?
test.why: Genesis 16 tells how the Angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring.

test.q: What did Moses see in Exodus 3?
choices: A bush that burned but did not burn up
test.why: Exodus 3 says Moses saw a bush that burned but was not burned up.

test.q: What did Heiser think about the Angel of the LORD?
choices: He was just a bright light
He was God himself, coming close
test.why: Heiser thought the Angel of the LORD was God himself, coming close so people could see.

test.q: Which angel brought good news to Mary?
test.why: Luke 1 says the angel Gabriel came to Mary.

test.q: What do angels often say in the stories?
test.why: In Luke, angels often say, "Do not be afraid."

choices: Special and set apart for God
test.why: Holy means special and set apart for God, like the ground by the bush.

test.q: In Matthew 28:19, where did Jesus send his friends?
test.why: Jesus sent his friends to all nations.

test.q: At Pentecost, how did the visitors hear the good news?
test.why: Acts 2 says each visitor heard in their own language.

test.q: Heiser saw Pentecost as the opposite of which story?
test.why: At Babel, languages sent people apart. Heiser saw Pentecost bringing them together.

choices: A crowd from every nation, all together
test.why: Revelation 7:9 pictures a crowd from every nation and language, standing together.

write.prompt: Pick two stories: Hagar (Genesis 16), Moses (Exodus 3), or Pentecost (Acts 2). Draw or tell what happened. Who came close? Who was welcomed? Say what Heiser thought.
tips: Name the book, like Genesis or Acts.
Tell the story in order: first, next, last.
Use one unit word, like messenger, holy or nation.
